# A Note on AI Assistance {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-warning title="Working draft: Unverified text"}
**This text is an active, evolving work in progress.** Unlike earlier foundational texts in this curriculum, which underwent multi-semester classroom adoption and extensive one-on-one expert peer review, **this text has not yet been independently or humanly validated**. It is an early draft shared openly to invite community feedback, critique, and collective refinement.
:::

This book is released as an open-access, living textbook; it is not yet under contract with a commercial publisher. In earlier works, systems and computing infrastructure was my native intellectual home. But *Physical AI* pushes across the causal boundary into unfamiliar terrain: classical kinematics, control barrier functions, actuator thermodynamics, and hard real-time latency budgets.

The central challenge in writing this book was conducting an exhaustive cross-disciplinary survey across fields that rarely speak to one another—robotics, control theory, mechanical engineering, and machine learning infrastructure. I used artificial intelligence extensively as an **interactive thinking and research partner** to explore unfamiliar dynamics, survey disparate literature, brainstorm structural framings, and distill foundational first principles. In assembling these chapters, I am using the process of working with AI as a personal learning vehicle to read, synthesize, and organize my own understanding of a vast and rapidly evolving domain.

However, in the physical world, errors carry kinetic consequences: delay is paid in millimeters, and unhandled failure results in mechanical damage or physical harm. For that very reason, **this unverified draft must be read with rigorous skepticism**. While our executable Python cells verify numerical consistency and continuous integration tests check reference hygiene, the systems architectures and safety abstractions presented here have not yet completed the rigorous, one-on-one human expert validation required for a definitive reference. That comprehensive review by robotics and control specialists is an ongoing process.

Authorship is thinking. Deciding which physical constraints belong in this curriculum, sequencing chapters so that Newtonian limits precede learned policies, and identifying where practitioners will encounter real-world traps are human judgment calls that no tool can make. The architectural synthesis and choices are mine.

Transparency is foundational to engineering ethics. I invite readers, roboticists, and systems engineers to read critically, report errors on GitHub, challenge the proposed models, and help us turn this working draft into a safe and verified foundation for embodied machine learning.

The principle holds with absolute finality at the physical boundary: **the tool can propose, and the tool can tutor, but only the human engineer can ratify and take responsibility.**
